title_en: Friends of Nature Environmental Research Institute, Chaoyang District, Beijing and All-China Environment Federation v. PetroChina Company Limited and PetroChina Company Limited Jilin Oilfield Branch — public interest environmental pollution litigation
ruling_gist_en: In environmental civil public interest litigation cases, when a social organization initiates a lawsuit by listing both the legal person's branch that committed the environmental pollution act and the legal person that established the branch as defendants, it shall be confirmed that the legal person is a proper defendant. When multiple courts have jurisdiction over the case, the special rules of environmental public interest litigation shall be followed, and the case shall be placed under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the pollution act was committed or where the damage occurred, so as to accurately ascertain the facts, determine liability in accordance with the law, and ensure timely and effective restoration of the damaged ecological environment.

full_text_en:
Beijing Chaoyang District Friends of Nature Environmental Research Institute and All-China Environment Federation v. PetroChina Company Limited and PetroChina Company Limited Jilin Oilfield Branch — Environmental Public Interest Litigation

【Ruling Summary】

In environmental civil public interest litigation cases, where a social organization brings a lawsuit jointly against a legal person's branch that has committed environmental pollution acts and the legal person establishing such branch, the legal person should be confirmed as a proper defendant. Where several courts have jurisdiction over a case, the special characteristics of environmental public interest litigation should be followed, and the case should be placed under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the polluting act was committed or where the damage occurred, so as to accurately ascertain the facts, determine liability in accordance with the law, and ensure timely and effective restoration of the damaged ecological environment.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2018) Supreme People's Court Min Zai No. 177

Re-applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Chaoyang District Friends of Nature Environmental Research Institute. Address: Room 406, Building 10 (Youcheng Building), No. 2 Qijia Huozi (South Courtyard), Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Boju, Director of the Institute.

Agent ad litem: Hu Yulai, lawyer at Beijing Huanming Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): PetroChina Company Limited. Address: No. 16 Ande Road, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wang Yilin, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yiping, lawyer at Beijing Hanlian United Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): PetroChina Company Limited Jilin Oilfield Branch. Address: No. 1219 Yanjiang East Road, Ningjiang District, Songyuan City, Jilin Province.

Head: Jiang Pengfei, General Manager of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Yiping, lawyer at Beijing Hanlian United Law Firm.

Appellant at Second Instance (Plaintiff at First Instance): All-China Environment Federation. Address: 6th Floor, Huabiao Building, Qingniangou East Road, Hepingli District 14, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yonghong, Secretary-General of the Federation.

The re-applicant Beijing Chaoyang District Friends of Nature Environmental Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Friends of Nature), due to a dispute over environmental pollution public interest litigation with the respondents PetroChina Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as PetroChina Company), PetroChina Company Limited Jilin Oilfield Branch (hereinafter referred to as PetroChina Jilin Branch), and the appellant at second instance All-China Environment Federation, unsatisfied with the civil ruling (2017) Jing Min Zhong No. 538 of the Beijing High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. After this Court ruled to bring the case for retrial, it formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the trial, and the trial has now been concluded.

Friends of Nature applied for retrial, alleging: (1) The civil ruling (2009) Min Shen Zi No. 389 of the Supreme People's Court cited by the second-instance ruling is not a guiding case and cannot be used as a basis for judgment, nor did that ruling clarify that PetroChina Company was not a proper defendant in that case. (2) Where a party raises an objection to jurisdiction, the people's court should first conduct a procedural review. However, the first-instance and second-instance courts conducted a substantive review of the defendant's qualification, which was clearly improper. (3) The "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases" (hereinafter referred to as the "Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation") clearly stipulates that the court at the defendant's domicile has jurisdiction. The first-instance and second-instance rulings violated the provisions of the judicial interpretation and should be corrected. Friends of Nature requested the revocation of the first-instance and second-instance rulings and that the case be tried lawfully by the Beijing No. 4 Intermediate People's Court.

PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch argued in defense: (1) PetroChina Jilin Branch has independent litigation subject qualifications. Friends of Nature's listing of PetroChina Jilin Branch and PetroChina Company as co-defendants has no legal basis and is contrary to legal principles. (2) The Supreme People's Court has, through numerous precedents, denied the practice of listing a legal person and its branch as co-defendants. The precedents provided by Friends of Nature listing a legal person and its branch as co-defendants are insufficient to support their claim. (3) It is not advisable for Friends of Nature to seek private gain by using environmental civil public interest litigation. (4) The review by the first-instance and second-instance courts of whether PetroChina Company was a proper defendant did not constitute a substantive trial. PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch requested the rejection of Friends of Nature's retrial request.

Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation filed a lawsuit at the first-instance court, requesting: (1) A judgment ordering PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch to immediately eliminate the danger by lawfully disposing of the dangerous waste in the seepage pit (approximately near North Latitude 44°33'57", East Longitude 124°17'00") located about two kilometers southwest of Dadeyingzi Village, Tuga Forest District, Wulantuga Forest Farm, Songyuan City, Jilin Province, and surrounding uncleared dangerous waste, the dangerous waste (including oil sludge buried underground and illegally placed oily soil) around Well Group 4 of the Oil Production Team 4 of Songyuan Gas Production Plant, and the dangerous waste and oily mud slurry in the seepage pit (approximately near North Latitude 44°33'35", East Longitude 124°16'39") located about two kilometers southwest of Dadeyingzi Village and surrounding areas, thereby eliminating the danger to the ecological environment such as soil and groundwater. (2) A judgment ordering PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch to immediately restore the condition to its original state, that is, to restore the soil and groundwater in the affected area due to the use of seepage pits by PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch to secretly discharge sewage to their original condition, and to restore the soil and groundwater affected by the oil sludge buried underground, oily mud slurry, and illegally placed oily soil to their original condition. (3) A judgment ordering PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch to compensate for the loss of service functions from the time the soil ecological environment was damaged until it is restored to its original condition (subject to the results of appraisal and assessment). (4) A judgment ordering PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch to make a public apology by publishing a notice of apology on national media for a period of no less than ten days. (5) A judgment ordering PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch to bear the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiffs due to the litigation and enforcement of this case, including travel expenses, investigation and evidence collection fees, expert witness fees, appraisal and assessment fees, lawyer fees, etc. (subject to the actual amount incurred). (6) The litigation costs of this case to be borne by PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch.

The first-instance court held: Article 6(1) of the Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation provides: "First-instance environmental civil public interest litigation cases shall be under the jurisdiction of the intermediate people's court or above at the place where the act of polluting the environment or damaging the ecology occurred, the place where the damage resulted, or the domicile of the defendant." As a branch established in accordance with the law and having obtained a business license, with certain organizational structure and property, PetroChina Jilin Branch falls within the scope of "other organizations" as stipulated in Article 48 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) and has the corresponding litigation subject qualification. Article 52 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law Judicial Interpretation) further clarifies: "The other organizations stipulated in Article 48 of the Civil Procedure Law refer to organizations that are lawfully established, have certain organizational structure and property, but do not have legal person status, including: ... (5) branches of a legal person that are lawfully established and have obtained a business license; ..." The company bears ultimate civil liability for the branch. If the branch's property is insufficient to satisfy debts, the company may be added as an enforcement subject during the enforcement stage of the case, and the company shall bear civil liability. This case is a dispute over liability for environmental pollution. As a branch, PetroChina Jilin Branch has the corresponding litigation subject qualification, can independently bear civil liability externally with its own property, and there is currently no evidence proving that PetroChina Company directly committed acts of polluting the environment or damaging the ecology. Therefore, PetroChina Company is not a proper defendant in this case. The first-instance court ruled: Rejecting Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation's lawsuit against PetroChina Company.

Friends of Nature, unsatisfied with the first-instance ruling, filed an appeal requesting that the first-instance ruling be revoked in accordance with the law.

The second-instance court found that PetroChina Company and PetroChina Jilin Branch both filed jurisdiction objection applications at first instance and submitted copies of legal documents including the Supreme People's Court civil ruling (2009) Min Shen Zi No. 389 as attachments to their jurisdiction objection applications. The Supreme People's Court civil ruling (2009) Min Shen Zi No. 389 reviewed the case of retrial applicant Bai Chunliang v. respondents PetroChina Company and PetroChina Company Limited Jilin Petrochemical Company concerning a dispute over compensation for infringement of rights of life, health, and bodily integrity, and held: "The subject of tort liability in this case is Jilin Petrochemical Company. The place of infringement is Jilin City, Jilin Province. Jilin Petrochemical Company is a branch of a legal person that is lawfully established, has obtained a business license, has certain organizational structure and property, and meets the statutory conditions for 'other organizations' under Article 49(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Jilin Petrochemical Company has the corresponding litigation subject qualification and can independently bear civil liability externally with its own property. To facilitate case trial and party litigation, the second-instance ruling dismissing Bai Chunliang's lawsuit was not improper. After obtaining relevant evidence, Bai Chunliang may file a compensation action with the people's court at the place where the infringement occurred." Consequently, it upheld the first-instance and second-instance rulings dismissing the plaintiff's lawsuit against PetroChina Company in that case.

The second-instance court held: This case is an environmental civil public interest litigation case. Article 6 of the Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation provides that first-instance environmental civil public interest litigation cases shall be under the jurisdiction of the intermediate people's court or above at the place where the act of polluting the environment or damaging the ecology occurred, the place where the damage resulted, or the domicile of the defendant. In this case, the first-instance court is the intermediate people's court at the domicile of PetroChina Company, not the court at the place where the act of polluting the environment occurred or the place where the damage resulted. Therefore, before a ruling on jurisdiction is made, it does not violate current legal provisions for the first-instance court to first make a determination on the issue of whether PetroChina Company is a proper subject. The situation in this case is entirely consistent with the litigation subject situation in the Supreme People's Court civil ruling (2009) Min Shen Zi No. 389: the subject that carried out the specific infringement act is a branch of a legal person that is lawfully established, has obtained a business license, and has certain organizational structure and property; the place of the infringement is at the domicile of that branch; the parties have filed a civil lawsuit jointly against that branch and the legal person that established it. In the presence of a precedent ruling, the second-instance court held that the first-instance ruling dismissing Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation's lawsuit against PetroChina Company was not improper and should be upheld. The second-instance court ruled: Appeal dismissed, original ruling upheld.

This Court holds: The issues in dispute in this case are, first, whether PetroChina Company is a proper defendant in this case; and second, how to determine the court with jurisdiction in this case to better facilitate the protection of the ecological environment.

(I) Regarding the issue of whether PetroChina Company is a proper defendant in this case

A branch of a legal person engages in civil activities in its own name, and the civil liability arising therefrom shall be borne by the legal person; it may also first be satisfied from the property managed by the branch, and if insufficient, shall be borne by the legal person. According to Article 48 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 52 of the Civil Procedure Law Judicial Interpretation, a branch of a legal person that is lawfully established, has obtained a business license, and has certain organizational structure and property may be a party to civil litigation. However, the issue of whether a plaintiff, when suing a branch of a legal person, may also jointly sue the legal person that established that branch is not explicitly addressed by relevant laws and judicial interpretations. Given that the purpose of granting other organizations the qualification of parties in civil litigation is to protect the civil rights of other organizations and counterparties and to resolve disputes in a timely manner, and there is no intention to restrict the plaintiff from jointly suing the legal person that established the branch, this matter, unless otherwise provided by laws and regulations, should be a procedural matter that the plaintiff may choose when filing the lawsuit.

This case is an environmental civil public interest litigation initiated by Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation regarding acts of polluting the environment by PetroChina Jilin Branch. Article 6(3) of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators shall prevent and reduce environmental pollution and ecological damage, and shall bear responsibility for the damage caused in accordance with the law." Article 5 of the Company Law provides: "When engaging in business activities, a company must comply with laws and administrative regulations, abide by social morality and business ethics, be honest and trustworthy, accept supervision from the government and the public, and assume social responsibility." Article 11 of the "Guiding Opinions of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council on Central Enterprises Fulfilling Social Responsibilities" also clearly states that "strengthening resource conservation and environmental protection" is an important social responsibility that central enterprises should assume. The petroleum industry is a typical resource- and energy-intensive industry. The entire petroleum chain, from extraction and refining to transportation and terminal sales, is highly prone to causing environmental pollution and ecological damage. This requires petroleum enterprises, while pursuing economic benefits, to take effective measures to prevent and control environmental pollution and ecological damage, maximize the protection of environmental public interests, and promote coordinated economic, social, and environmental development. As a large petroleum enterprise directly managed by the central government, PetroChina Company should consciously assume and supervise its branches to assume corresponding responsibilities for ecological and environmental protection. Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation, by initiating environmental civil public interest litigation due to environmental pollution and listing PetroChina Jilin Branch and PetroChina Company as co-defendants, has a positive role in urging PetroChina Company to further strengthen the supervision of its branches and actively assume social responsibility for safeguarding environmental public interests. The second-instance court's use of a retrial review ruling in another case as a precedent to dismiss Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation's lawsuit against PetroChina Company lacks sufficient legal basis and is not conducive to achieving the purpose of the environmental public interest litigation system, and should be corrected.

(II) Regarding the issue of how to determine the court with jurisdiction in this case to better facilitate the protection of the ecological environment

Article 28 of the Civil Procedure Law provides: "A lawsuit arising from a tort shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the place where the tort was committed or where the defendant has its domicile." Article 6 of the Environmental Civil Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation provides: "First-instance environmental civil public interest litigation cases shall be under the jurisdiction of the intermediate people's court or above at the place where the act of polluting the environment or damaging the ecology occurred, the place where the damage resulted, or the domicile of the defendant." According to the above provisions, both the Beijing No. 4 Intermediate People's Court (domicile of PetroChina Company) and the Songyuan Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province (domicile of PetroChina Jilin Branch and place where the polluting act occurred and damage resulted) have jurisdiction over this case.

This case is an environmental civil public interest litigation case. The core objective of environmental civil public interest litigation is to promote the restoration of damaged ecological environments. It should implement restorative justice concepts and follow certain special trial rules. This is mainly reflected in the following: the people's court needs to conduct on-site inspections at the pollution site as soon as possible after accepting the case, deeply understand the facts of damage to the ecological environment, and make preliminary judgments on whether to take measures such as evidence preservation and act preservation to avoid the continuation and expansion of pollution; it needs to notify relevant departments responsible for environmental protection supervision and management of the case acceptance information, provide clues for environmental administrative law enforcement, and promote the timely initiation of administrative enforcement; it needs to ensure the public's, especially residents near the pollution site, right to know, participate, and supervise environmental public interest litigation by publishing acceptance announcements and openly trying the case with a collegial panel composed of people's assessors; it needs to communicate and coordinate with relevant departments on matters such as evidence collection, damage assessment, determination of restoration plans, and introduction of third-party institutions. After the judgment takes effect, the people's court also needs to supervise the ecological environment restoration work to a certain extent to ensure that the restoration costs borne by the polluter are used for ecological environmental protection. Given that the trial of environmental public interest litigation cases is closely related to the ecological environment to be protected, jurisdiction by a people's court far from the place of the polluting act and the place of damage is not convenient for the trial, is not conducive to the timely and effective restoration of the damaged ecological environment, and makes it difficult to achieve the core objective of promoting ecological environment restoration in environmental public interest litigation. In this case, the polluting acts alleged by Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation were carried out by PetroChina Jilin Branch, whose domicile is located in Songyuan City, Jilin Province. The pollution sites are concentrated within the jurisdiction of Songyuan City, Jilin Province. The main litigation requests are to remove pollution, restore the environment, etc. This Court holds: Considering the special characteristics of environmental public interest litigation and the actual circumstances of this case, trial of this case by the Songyuan Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province is convenient for the people's court to conduct the trial and for the parties to litigate, is conducive to accurately ascertaining the facts of the case, lawfully determining the liability of the parties, and promoting the effective restoration of the damaged ecological environment.

In summary, the first-instance and second-instance rulings in this case, which dismissed Friends of Nature and All-China Environment Federation's lawsuit against PetroChina Company, were erroneous in the application of the law, and this Court hereby corrects them. In accordance with Article 207(1), Article 170(1)(ii), and Article 37(1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 407(2) and Article 332 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2017) Jing Min Zhong No. 538 of the Beijing High People's Court and the civil ruling (2016) Jing 04 Min Chu No. 122 of the Beijing No. 4 Intermediate People's Court are revoked;

2. This case shall be tried by the Songyuan Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province.

This ruling is final.
